My wife and I have been working out consistently for the past 3 years. When we started we were both overweight by about 40-50 lbs. Some keys things we have found:

  1. Cardio is not necessary. We both hated it and prefer lifting. Cardio burns calories while you work out then it's done. Lifting weights burns less at the moment, but over then next couple of days it continues to burn calories. It actually takes quiet a bit of energy for the body to repair muscle from lifting and in the end it has about the same net loss of calories. Cardio will also burn lean muscle after a certain amount and this is not what we want. Most people who lift and do cardio try to keep the cardio sessions around 20 minutes a day to avoid this.

  2. Find a routine and stick to it. Stronglifts 5x5 is a good program. PPL (Push Pull Legs) is my personal favorite. You can find both easily on Google. You will not become a huge man looking monster! It can't happen. You can lift heavy weight daily like Arnie and you will never get big. Ever. Lean and cut, yes, but not huge muscle. For a female to achieve such a look it take steroids.

  3. Use proper form! If you don't know what you are doing find out. You can hire a personal trainer, or find someone you know who lifts. YouTube is an unbelievable wealth of form knowledge. Even if you think you know how something is done or you see others doing it a certain way, look it up. Scott Herman is my person favorite YouTube guy for form checks. You can type in Herman seated row for example and get a quick clip on how to do that exercise. He has about any exercise you could imagine. He isn't the only who makes videos though and I'm sure there are tons of other good people on there.

  4. Try to keep your exercises to 50-60 minutes a day.

  5. Lifting is hard but rewarding work. Your exercise should be taxing.

  6. Exercising should be a way of life. Don't set goals of this weight, or that. Don't think of crossing a finish line. If you lose the weight and gain the appearance you want you are still not done. It is forever. It is a gift you want to be able to perform till death. If you take this mindset, and have a little luck, you can be like my 72 year old father who still works out with me to this day and works side by side with me at hard labor projects.

  7. This is the biggest thing most people never understand. You don't have to lift or do any cardio to lose weight at all. Losing weight is do to decreasing caloric intake. Count your calories with a tracker like Myfitnesspal app. find out what your TDEE is and set your goal around -500 calories of that. 1/2 to 1 pound a week is usually the best rate.

Congrats on the progress and keep it up! You are doing something that most people just are not able to accomplish. Be proud of that!

Basically I'm here to start things off. I'm in my early 40s, recently divorced. I've had a long history of a variety of addictions - porn, pot, gambling, and pills were the main ones. Maybe alcohol. I've gotten clean with the help of LifeRing Secular Recovery and recently celebrated my two year sobriety anniversary - which is pretty awesome!

My ex is an alcoholic in recovery. She does 12-step. Let's just say we had a toxic relationship and without really even being completely aware of it - we enabled the worst aspects of each other. Life is much better divorced and separated from her. I have a girlfriend now (who is neither an addict nor in recovery herself - she has never done drugs and has a glass of wine maybe once a month), and I attend one Lifering meeting per week, which keeps me straight.

I'm here because I'm excited about Voat - I think it's the brave new world of threaded discussions! ANYTHING goes here. Also, I noticed on Reddit that they never really did addiction recovery right. They had /r/alcohol and nothing else, really, for people who wanted recovery resources. Also, those /r/alcohol folks seemed pretty narrowly focused on 12-step. While I'm very welcoming and happy to chat with 12-step folks, I don't want this to be a forum where the 12-steps are considered the default form of recovery with the exclusion of all others.

Also, finally, I am happy to discuss harm reduction or moderation with folks as well. While I do not practice moderation or harm reduction (I tried it for years - got sick of it), I am completely supportive of those that are into that kind of thing, and I think it's a perfectly legitimate way to go. If it works for you, why not?

Welcome. I'll add some more links and discussion threads here when I am in the mood, later on.
